title: Enterprise Risk Management
overview: Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) has advanced significantly since its inception in the 1970s. Initially focused on purchasing insurance, ERM has grown into a critical organizational function that integrates with Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC). This comprehensive system begins with corporate governance and culminates in compliance, ensuring that risks are systematically identified, assessed, and mitigated to help organizations achieve their objectives.

This course is based on the globally recognized ERM framework designed by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO). Participants will explore the step-by-step process of controlling risk, starting with evaluating the internal environment, setting objectives aligned with corporate vision and governance, and identifying and responding to risks effectively. The course also addresses risk monitoring, communication, and reporting, with a focus on various organizational and industry-specific risk categories, such as strategic, operational, financial, and compliance risks
audience: This course is designed for managers, senior managers, directors, executives, financial controllers, senior finance and accounting personnel, and auditors seeking to enhance their understanding of ERM practices.
methodology: The course employs a blend of detailed instructor-led sessions, participant presentations, and interactive case studies drawn from diverse industries and business functions.
competencies: Advising boards and executives on risk strategies
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Identify internal and external factors that introduce risks to the organization.
Enhance Risk-Based Decision-Making (RBDM) and strengthen governance collaboration with the board of directors.
Develop and influence internal controls based on identified risks.
Categorize organizational risks and assign appropriate authorities to manage them.
Analyze, assess, and improve risk management practices within their organizations.

items.text: Internal and external environmental changes influencing risk
The GRC framework: Governance, Risk, and Compliance
Integration of risk management into corporate governance
Case studies of governance failures and lessons learned
The role of risk management in designing internal controls
Historical development and benefits of ERM
ERM platforms and their applications in:
External risks, including socioeconomic, regulatory, technological, and competitive factors
Internal risks, including organizational structure, processes, and culture
Internal Environment: Setting the foundation for risk management
Objective Setting: Aligning risk management with organizational goals
Event Identification: Detecting potential risk triggers
Control Activities: Implementing measures to address risks
Information and Communication: Ensuring clear risk communication
Risk Monitoring: Continuously tracking and refining risk management processes
